import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

def get_left (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ l _ => some l
  | _ => none

def get_right (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ r => some r
  | _ => none

def get_val (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v _ _ => some v
  | _ => none

def BinarySearchTree.is_node (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ _ => True
  | _ => False

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zigzig_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t ∧ 
  BinarySearchTree.is_node t ∧ 
  (match get_left t with 
   | some p => BinarySearchTree.is_node p ∧ 
               (match get_left p with 
                | some x => BinarySearchTree.is_node x 
                | none => False)
   | none => False)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def zigzigAux (t : BinarySearchTree) : BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node gv (BinarySearchTree.Node pv (BinarySearchTree.Node xv a b) c) d =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node xv a (BinarySearchTree.Node pv b (BinarySearchTree.Node gv c d))
  | _ => t
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def zigzig (t : BinarySearchTree) 
    (h_precond : zigzig_precond t) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  zigzigAux t
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zigzig_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : zigzig_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∧
  -- Structural properties: X (grandchild) is now root
  get_val result = get_val (get_left (get_left t).get!).get!
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem zigzig_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree)
    (h_precond : zigzig_precond t) :
    zigzig_postcond t (zigzig t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  revert h_precond
  cases t with
  | Empty =>
    intro h
    exact ((h.2.1 : False)).elim
  | Node gv l d =>
    cases l with
    | Empty =>
      intro h
      exact ((h.2.2.1 : False)).elim
    | Node pv l2 c =>
      cases l2 with
      | Empty =>
        intro h
        exact ((h.2.2.2 : False)).elim
      | Node xv a b =>
        intro h
        have hres :
            zigzig (BinarySearchTree.Node gv
              (BinarySearchTree.Node pv (BinarySearchTree.Node xv a b) c) d) h
            = BinarySearchTree.Node xv a
                (BinarySearchTree.Node pv b (BinarySearchTree.Node gv c d)) := rfl
        rw [hres]
        have hbst : is_bst (BinarySearchTree.Node gv
            (BinarySearchTree.Node pv (BinarySearchTree.Node xv a b) c) d) := h.1
        simp only [is_bst, view] at hbst
        obtain ⟨hL, ⟨hX, ⟨ha, hbsta, hb, hbstb⟩, hc, hbstc⟩, hd, hbstd⟩ := hbst
        have hpg : pv < gv := hL pv (by simp)
        have hxp : xv < pv := hX xv (by simp)
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, rfl⟩
        · simp only [is_bst, view]
          refine ⟨ha, hbsta, ?_, ?_, hbstb, ?_, ?_, hbstc, hd, hbstd⟩
          · intro y hy
            simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff, or_assoc] at hy
            rcases hy with h1 | h1 | h1 | h1 | h1
            · exact hb y h1
            · have := hc y h1; linarith
            · have := hd y h1; linarith
            · subst h1; linarith
            · subst h1; linarith
          · intro y hy
            refine hX y ?_
            simp only [Set.mem_union]
            exact Or.inl (Or.inr hy)
          · intro y hy
            simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff, or_assoc] at hy
            rcases hy with h1 | h1 | h1
            · exact hc y h1
            · have := hd y h1; linarith
            · subst h1; linarith
          · intro y hy
            refine hL y ?_
            simp only [Set.mem_union]
            exact Or.inl (Or.inr hy)
        · simp only [view]
          ext y
          simp only [Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          tauto
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## Analysis

**The operation.** A zig‑zig (double right rotation) applies to a tree of shape

```
t = Node g (Node p (Node x A B) C) D
```

and produces

```
result = Node x A (Node p B (Node g C D))
```

**Why it's correct.**

*Set preservation:* both trees contain exactly `A ∪ B ∪ C ∪ D ∪ {x,p,g}`, so the views are equal (pure set algebra).

*BST invariant:* from `is_bst t` we get `x < p` (since `x ∈ view (Node x A B)` and everything there is `< p`) and `p < g` (since `p ∈ view (Node p … C)` and everything there is `< g`). Then:
- `A < x` ✓, `B > x` ✓,
- `C > p > x`, `D > g > p > x`, `g > p > x`, `p > x`, giving the right subtree bound for `x`;
- `B < p`, `C > p`, `D > g > p` giving the bounds for `p`;
- `C < g`, `D > g` giving the bounds for `g`.

*Structural:* the root value of the result is literally `x`, which is `get_val (get_left (get_left t).get!).get!` — true by `rfl`.

**Plan.** Define an auxiliary total function `zigzigAux` (identity on non‑matching shapes), let `zigzig` be it. In the proof, case-split on the tree; the three degenerate shapes contradict the precondition (definitional `False`), and in the good case we unfold `is_bst`/`view` and discharge the arithmetic side conditions with `linarith` and the set equality with `tauto`.

- Original: `G(P(X(a,b), c), d)`
- Result: `X(a, P(b, G(c,d)))`

Thus:

- `X` becomes the new root.
- `P` becomes the right child of `X`.
- `G` becomes the right child of `P`.
- All four subtrees `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d` remain in their correct relative positions.
